title: Deterministic finalization for orphaned streaming fragments and late acknowledgements
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: In long-lived streaming sessions we observe nondeterministic billing outcomes when fragments are produced but not finalized due to client disconnects, mid-stream model handoffs, or late ACKs from relay/proxy layers. This leads to two classes of incorrectness: 1) under-crediting (customer gets charged less but server state is left inconsistent) and 2) over-crediting (duplicate credits when resumed fragments are re-sent). Both cause refunds, manual audits, and customer trust issues. Existing heuristics (time TTLs + best-effort reconciliation) are brittle under high churn and do not guarantee idempotent final billing decisions.
proposal: Introduce a deterministic finalization workflow for streaming fragments: (a) attach a compact, monotonically increasing fragment sequence + stream-id + idempotency token to every fragment; (b) issue provisional credits at fragment emission time and record them in the 'provisional ledger'; (c) accept an explicit 'finalize' marker (finalization record) that atomically moves a contiguous sequence range from provisional -> committed credits for that stream; (d) if finalization does not arrive within a TTL, run a deterministic tombstone job that emits a finalization decision using a deterministic policy (e.g., favor consumer-provided sequencing when valid, otherwise apply server-side truncation rules). The system will surface provisional vs committed breakdowns in billing dashboards and expose a reconciliation report for audits.
design_notes:
- Ledger: add a compact per-stream ledger table with rows: stream_id (pk), last_committed_seq, last_provisional_seq, tombstone_state, last_updated. The ledger stores minimal summary so lookups are O(1) on finalize.
- Finalize API: POST /streams/{id}/finalize with payload {upto_seq, idempotency_key, signature?}. Idempotent: re-finalizing same upto_seq is a noop.
- Provisional credits: credits are reserved in a provisional bucket keyed by (customer_id, billing_window, provisional_tag). Committed finalization clears provisional_tag and moves tokens to billable totals.
- Reconnect semantics: client supplies resume_token; server validates seq monotonicity and rejects duplicates. On mismatched sequences, server returns a concise delta and requires re-send of missing fragments with same idempotency tokens.
- Deterministic tombstone job: runs at N seconds after last_provisional_seq update; computes finalization boundary using recorded last received seq and a conservative policy (e.g., commit only contiguous prefix), emits finalize(upto_seq) on behalf of stream. This is deterministic given the ledger state.
- Tradeoffs: introduces slight latency in when credits are considered final (until finalize/tombstone), but avoids double-charging and allows cheaper provisional accounting bookkeeping. Requires DB guarantees for atomic move of provisional -> committed.
acceptance_criteria: Provisionally credited fragments are visible in the provisional bucket within 200ms of emission
Finalize call atomically moves contiguous fragment range from provisional to committed with no observable duplication in billing for 1000 simulated reconnect scenarios
Tombstone job deterministically finalizes orphaned streams and matches the reconcile harness expected output in >99.99% of synthetic trials
No increase in 95th percentile billing latency beyond 5% for typical streaming workloads in canary cluster
Dashboards surface provisional vs committed token counts per stream and per-customer
End-to-end billing audits (PRD link) can reconcile charges to ledger entries for a 30-day sample without manual adjustments
tasks: Schema: add ledger table + provisional bucket metadata and migrations
API: implement /streams/{id}/finalize endpoint and client SDK helpers
Runtime: emit fragment metadata (seq, idempotency_key) from serving path
Worker: implement tombstone deterministic finalizer with configurable TTL
Billing: implement atomic move from provisional -> committed and update token counters
Observability: add provisional/committed metrics, SLO, and alerting rules
Tests: unit, integration, chaos tests for reconnects and midstream model switch
Docs & SDK: document resume semantics and add examples to streaming SDK
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for ledger transitions and finalize idempotency. 2) Integration tests with local streaming harness that simulates disconnects, reordered fragments, and duplicate sends. 3) Reconciliation suite: run the new finalizer vs existing heuristic reconciler over historical traces and assert deterministic outcomes. 4) Chaos tests: introduce packet drops and delayed ACKs in staging canary; validate no duplicate committed credits. 5) Billing audit: generate synthetic workload across 10k streams and verify final invoice totals match committed ledger sums. 6) Run rate-limit soak to verify no regression in token reservation performance.
rollout_plan: Feature-gate with runtime flag. Stage 1: unit + integration done. Stage 2: internal canary (infra teams) on staging cluster for 2 weeks. Stage 3: 5% of production traffic from low-risk customers with audit logging enabled. Stage 4: expand to 50% then 100% after 7-day stability checks. Rollback: disable finalizer flag to resume legacy TTL heuristic and run compensating reconciliation. Monitor: provisional/committed ratio, reconciliation errors, billing complaints channel.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: DB contention when moving provisional -> committed at high volume. Mitigation: sharded provisional buckets, use batched atomic updates, rate-limit finalizer concurrency.
- Risk: Clients not sending idempotency tokens causing ambiguous fragments. Mitigation: server will synthesize stable idempotency keys for any fragment with missing token and emit warning metrics; require SDK update for long-term.
- Risk: Tombstone policy chooses wrong boundary and under/over credits. Mitigation: make tombstone policy configurable per-customer and expose dry-run mode used by billing team before enabling.

parent_issue_notes: This ticket implements a deterministic reconciliation primitive relied on by the higher-level midstream model handoff work.
notes: This approach favors correctness and auditability over immediate final billing; provisional credits are visible to customers and will be reconciled in the same billing window to minimize confusion. Follow-up tickets will address SDK ergonomics and operator tooling for manual dispute resolution.
